# Lisa Cirenza

> Lisa Cirenza is a painter in the French Alps. Shaped by her time as a young researcher on the Juneau Icefield, she paints light, water, rock and time (ice, snow, fog, lake and mountains) in encaustic, mixed media, oil and watercolour. She founded Espace Créa-Tea-Vité, a gallery, tea room and studio in La Clusaz (Haute-Savoie, France), where she teaches and hosts painting retreats. English is the official language of this site; a French version lives under /fr.

## About

Lisa Cirenza is a painter based in the French Alps. As a National Science Foundation scholar with the Juneau Icefield Research Program, she worked as a field researcher on glaciological expeditions across the Juneau Icefield, and later co-authored The Power of Ice, a children's book on glaciers and field science illustrated with her expedition photographs. She studied applied earth sciences at Stanford University and the École des Mines de Paris, and holds a master's in international policy studies from Stanford. Trained in old-masters oil technique and in sumi ink in Japan, she works with water, pigments, heat and wax. After years of painting people and the forces that divide them, from commuters on the London Underground to refugees, she now paints light, water, rock and time. Her work is held in the Stanford Hospital collection alongside works by David Hockney and Robert Rauschenberg, and in private collections in Europe, the United States and Asia. It has been praised in the Financial Times, and exhibited at the Grand Palais in Paris, in Venice during the Biennale, at the Asian Art Biennale in Dhaka, and in New York, Miami, London, Kyoto and Xi'an. She is a Sociétaire of the Salon d'Automne in Paris.

- Current series: A Record of Time. Earlier series (London Underground, refugees, digital work, Cuba) are in the Archive.
- Statement, in her words: "Most people look up and see the Alps. I see a record of time, still being written, and light coaxing new life from every layer."
- She was a field researcher on the Juneau Icefield, not a glaciologist.
- Venice: Personal Structures, European Cultural Centre, Palazzo Mora, during the 59th Venice Biennale.
